_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: idx 2, 4, 6 ONLY. Full page map, all 8 accounted for: idx0 = cover (bilingual, 'Page 1 of 8'); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + Q1-6; idx3 = HINDI Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11; idx4 = ENGLISH Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11; idx5 = HINDI Q12-14; idx6 = ENGLISH Q12-14; idx7 = 'Page 8 of 8', BLANK apart from QR code and footer. The booklet is chunked Hindi-then-English per block, NOT page-alternating end-to-end, so English is idx 2/4/6 and there are only three English pages. NO overflow of one language onto the other's page: every Hindi page ends on a completed question (idx1 ends at Q6, idx3 at Q11(b), idx5 at Q14(ii)) and every English page likewise, so no English text sits at the top of any odd index. Verified page-by-page rather than assumed. STRUCTURE (printed General Instructions, idx2): three Sections; A = Q1-6 short answer type-I @2, B = Q7-10 short answer type-II @3, C = Q11-14 long answer @4, with (vii) Q14 a case based problem with 2 subparts of 2 marks each. Marks sum 12+12+16 = 40, matching the cover's Maximum Marks : 40 and 14 questions. NO MCQs anywhere in the paper - every question is subjective, so no options, no answer letters, and no blind key re-derivation applies. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so the count was established by reading, then confirmed question-by-question against the official marking scheme, which reprints both branches. FOUR internal choices: Q3, Q7, Q9, Q11 - each printed (a) / OR / (b). Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q10, Q12, Q13, Q14 carry no alternative. 19 rows = 14 questions + 4 OR-alternatives + 1 extra case-study sub-part. SYLLABUS NOTE: this is the COVID-era Term-2 paper set on the PRE-rationalisation syllabus, and Q6 and Q8 both examine the PLANE in 3-D, which rationalised NCERT Ch.11 no longer teaches - there is no 'plane' subtopic on the live axis, so both are filed on the closest subtopic and _flag'd. No sibling 2023-2026 paper in this corpus has a 3-D plane question.

questions.subtopic: Order and Degree of a Differential Equation
questions.stem: Find the sum of the order and the degree of the differential equation : \(\left(x + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 1\)
In a parallelogram PQRS, \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\) and \(\overrightarrow{PS} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{k}\). Find \(|\overrightarrow{PR}|\) and \(|\overrightarrow{QS}|\).
If \(\frac{d}{dx}[F(x)] = \frac{\sec^4 x}{\operatorname{cosec}^4 x}\) and \(F\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4}\), then find \(F(x)\).
Let A and B be two events such that \(P(A) = \frac{5}{8}\), \(P(B) = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(P(A/B) = \frac{3}{4}\). Find the value of \(P(B/A)\).
Two balls are drawn at random from a bag containing 2 red balls and 3 blue balls, without replacement. Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls. Find the probability distribution of X.
questions._flag: Printed as 'Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls' - the printed subject-verb agreement is wrong ('denotes' for 'denote'). Transcribed as printed; the question is unambiguous.

questions.stem: Find the values of \(\lambda\), for which the distance of point \((2, 1, \lambda)\) from plane \(3x + 5y + 4z = 11\) is \(2\sqrt{2}\) units.

If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) and \(\vec{d}\) are four non-zero vectors such that \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{d}\) and \(\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = 4\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\), then show that \((\vec{a} - 2\vec{d})\) is parallel to \((2\vec{b} - \vec{c})\) where \(\vec{a} \neq 2\vec{d}\), \(\vec{c} \neq 2\vec{b}\).

The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by \(2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\). Find the unit vectors parallel to its diagonals. Using the diagonal vectors, find the area of the parallelogram also.

Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot (2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) = 7\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot (2\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = 9\) and through the point \((2, 1, 3)\).
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x\frac{dy}{dx} + x\cos^2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = y\); given that when \(x = 1\), \(y = \frac{\pi}{4}\).

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region \(\{(x, y) : 4x^2 + 9y^2 \leq 36, 2x + 3y \geq 6\}\).
Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by lines \(x - y + 1 = 0\), \(x = -2\), \(x = 3\) and \(x\)-axis.

A card from a pack of 52 playing cards is lost. From the remaining cards, 2 cards are drawn at random without replacement, and are found to be both aces. Find the probability that lost card being an ace.
questions._flag: Printed as 'Find the probability that lost card being an ace.' - the printed phrasing is ungrammatical (no article, participial 'being'). Transcribed as printed; the intent is unambiguous.

questions.context:
Electrical transmission wires which are laid down in winters are stretched tightly to accommodate expansion in summers.
Two such wires lie along the following lines :
\(l_1 : \frac{x + 1}{3} = \frac{y - 3}{-2} = \frac{z + 2}{-1}\)
\(l_2 : \frac{x}{-1} = \frac{y - 7}{3} = \frac{z + 7}{-2}\)
Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Are the lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) coplanar ? Justify your answer.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a captioned photograph of an electrical transmission tower (labels: Grounded metal tower, Overhead ground wires, Nearest three phase conductors, Insulators). It carries no data; both line equations are printed in the text. Page idx 6.
